full_judgment: 29. The circumstantial evidence must be shown that the circumstance is as such the only conclusion can be drawn about the implication of the accused and nothing else. But here in the case we find mere probability and the learned trial Court on conjecture and surmises found that on such probability presumption can be drawn about the complicity of the accused applicant making a third case of his own. But law does not provide that any presumption or probability can be -the basis of conviction and sentence. If probability of involvement of the accused, mayor may not be, when these two views can be presumed, then in such case it cannot be taken into consideration as evidence. It appears, that the defence case of the appellant has been put to the PWs during their cross examination that there were two unions and he belonged to one union and others including High Officials belonged to other rival union and as such, crept up enmity with the High Officials. Another most important aspect as pointed out by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the appellant was in Traffic of Biman and naturally he was known to Customs Officials, the Civil Aviation employees and others who were employees in the Airport but not a single witness from amongst those persons and not even anybody from Traffic of Biman appeared before the court to say that on that particular date and particular time accused appellant was at the tarmac. There are some Exts produced and marked Exts, in the case i.e. a letter to the DGM Biman. It appears that the Investigating Officer did not care to go to Biman Office in the capacity of Investigating Officer of the case but sent a letter to the DGM Biman which has been marked as exhibit and the reply of the DGM which have also been marked as Exhibits 14 and 15 respectively but we fail to understood how at least Ext. 15 can be evidence without examination of the author of it, the DGM Biman.
